question.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 7 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

Notice that the $2$nd column of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 0 \\ 10 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 0 \\ 10 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd column of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =2|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 0 \\ 10 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 7 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =4|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 7 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(15+21) \\  & =144.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|144|=144.
$$
